components.name: Primary Button

components.name: Secondary Button

narrative.overview: A pocket coach for serious cribbage players. The visual system is built around one premise: the user is here on purpose, holding the phone in one hand, running through hands deliberately. Every screen is a single decision space. Color stays out of the way until the math has a verdict to deliver. Typography honors the source material (real cards have serif ranks) without leaning into card-game cliché. Soft ambient depth throughout, never theatrical lift. The product side of the personality is Raycast's discipline (one task per screen, quiet chrome, the work is the foreground). The brand side is Duolingo's loop (small, repeated wins; the reward arrives at the moment of feedback, not before). This system explicitly rejects the green-felt Vegas table, the bubble-button mobile game, generic SaaS dashboards, and brutalist statement work.
keyCharacteristics: Dark by default, light supported. The default user is studying on a phone after dinner.
One accent. Marker Gold is the only chromatic color in the chrome.
Serif for cards and totals, sans for chrome. The rank on a card and the score that came from those cards are the same typographic voice.
Mobile-thumb-first. Primary actions live in the bottom third; safe-area insets are non-negotiable.
Tactile components. 10–18px radii, generous padding, soft shadows. Friendly without being childish.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Marker Gold appears on ≤10% of any given screen and on at most one logical region at a time. Its rarity is the point.

rules.name: The Suit Quarantine Rule
rules.body: Red and Blue suit colors exist on playing-card surfaces only, never on buttons, never on text, never on dividers.

rules.name: The No-Pure-Black, No-Pure-White Rule
rules.body: The darkest value is #111111; tinted neutrals throughout. Body text is never #fff on dark, never #000 on light.

rules.name: The Serif-for-Substance Rule
rules.body: Playfair is reserved for card ranks, score totals, app title. Sans handles everything else. The serif is a signal that the user is looking at game material, not UI.

rules.name: The Letterspaced-Cap Label Rule
rules.body: Small labels (≤11px) are always uppercase with 0.08em letter-spacing.

rules.name: The Cards-Float, Chrome-Doesn't Rule
rules.body: Only playing cards cast meaningful shadows. UI chrome is flat at rest and uses tonal layering for depth.

rules.name: The No-Hover-Lift Rule
rules.body: Buttons do not translate up on hover. Hover changes background tint, never position.

dos: Do use Marker Gold (#f5b800) at ≤10% per screen, on one logical region at a time.
Do use Playfair Display for card ranks, score totals, and the screen title. Sans-serif everywhere else.
Do keep the playing card's center suit glyph at 24–30px so it reads from arm's length.
Do show the suit glyph (♠♥♦♣) every time suit color is used, so color-blind users are never blocked.
Do treat the bottom of the mobile screen as primary real estate. Sticky dock, safe-area insets, primary actions within thumb reach.
Do use 10–12px radii on chrome and 7px on playing cards.
Do ease motion out with cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) over 150–200ms.
Do maintain WCAG AA contrast across both themes.
donts: Don't use side-stripe borders as a colored accent on cards, list items, or nav items. The current NavDrawer active-item left stripe is a documented violation pending replacement.
Don't introduce a second chromatic chrome color. There is one accent (Marker Gold).
Don't ship green felt, gold gradients, ornate borders, or any other Vegas-casino motif.
Don't ship cartoon mascots, rainbow celebrations, or bubble-button drop shadows.
Don't ship identical card grids of icon-plus-heading-plus-text.
Don't ship modal dialogs as a first-resort UI. The drawer pattern is the only overlay pattern the system commits to.
Don't translate buttons on hover. Hover shifts background tint only.
Don't use em dashes in copy.
Don't use gradient text or background-clip: text.
